correctness.rationale: For \(k\ge3\), connectivity is equivalent to the two-state response map \(F(i)=R(C(i))\) being constant. The proof establishes both directions and computes \(\Pr(F\text{ constant})=(k+1)/(2k)\) and \(\Pr(\text{NE exists})=(3k+1)/(4k)\), yielding \(2(k+1)/(3k+1)\). The standalone exhaustive verifier directly constructs the graph for k=3,...,7; it corroborates but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source studies the same graph-connectivity definition but states its asymptotic theorem for equal action counts. Its model section notes that unequal action counts can be accommodated but the analysis is restricted for simplicity. The exact \(2\times k\) conditional formula and its \(2/3\) limit are derived for the distinct fixed-two-action regime. Prior sequential-dynamics results use a different convergence criterion. Residual risk remains for uninspected rectangular-action results outside the searched sources.

A prior exact theorem for rectangular-action ordinal games may exist outside the searched sources; the published-finding corpus partition and web-visible literature do not prove universal novelty.

value.rationale: The fixed-two-action regime is a natural and sharply different asymptotic regime for random games with unequal action-space sizes. The exact finite-\(k\) conditional fraction and its \(2/3\) limit show that the equal-action two-player vanishing limit cannot be transferred to this asymmetric setting; this is useful when interpreting connectivity for games with one low-cardinality player.
